deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Grothendieck works with an arrangement of pseudolines in the projective plane, with K its cell complex (vertices s, edges a). On the previous page he attaches to each vertex s a set Z_s, obtained as a quotient of the set of oriented pseudolines not through s, with a surjection compatible with the sign action ±1.

The natural reading of Z_s is the two-element set of local orientations of the plane at s. The complement of a pseudoline Δ is an open disk containing s. An orientation of Δ lifts to the boundary circle of that disk (which covers Δ twice) and so orients the disk.

For an edge a from s to s' he wants a transport bijection φ_a : Z_s → Z_{s'}. It is defined through the oriented pseudolines J that avoid both s and s'. The consistency condition (A9) says the two quotients of J agree: two oriented pseudolines avoiding s and s' that induce the same orientation at s' also induce the same orientation at s. Glued together, these φ_a form the combinatorial orientation local system (orientation double cover) of the projective plane, read off from the arrangement.

This page handles the degenerate case where no pseudoline avoids both s and s'. Then J is empty and φ_a cannot be defined that way. His workaround goes around a triangle:
- Let Θ be the pseudoline carrying a.
- Choose D ≠ Θ through s and D' ≠ Θ through s'. Then D ≠ D', since only Θ passes through both s and s'.
- Let t = D ∩ D', and let K' be the 3-line sub-arrangement {Θ, D, D'}. It has 3 vertices and cuts the plane into 4 triangles (figure 33).
- Pick b, one of the two segments of D from s to t.
- There is then a unique segment b' of D' from t to s' such that a, b, b' bound a triangle of K'.
- In K, b and b' are not single edges but chains of K-edges.
- The next page sets φ_a (written v_a) = v_{b'} ∘ v_b, composing the transports along those K-edges.

He flags the configuration where D and D' fail to exist, i.e. K is n ≥ 3 concurrent pseudolines through a single point (a pencil, where every edge is a loop at s). He seems to exclude it or treat it apart. On the next page he admits he has not checked that the definition is independent of the choices. He suggests treating the near-pencil (n concurrent lines cut by one more line) separately.

Aim. Encode the orientation data (the non-trivial orientation local system of the projective plane) purely combinatorially, in terms of (K, (R_i)), for arrangements coming from a space X.
errors: Independence of the choices (D, D', b) is not proved; Grothendieck says so himself on the next page.

The detour argument is potentially circular. The K-edges making up b and b' may themselves be edges with no pseudoline avoiding both endpoints, which happens in the near-pencil. So v_b and v_{b'} may not be defined yet; some induction or ordering is needed.

The degenerate cases (pencil; near-pencil; the case the next page calls a 'digon') are only sketched. In a pure pencil every edge is a loop at the single vertex s, so the construction (and Z_s itself) breaks down.

ideas.what: Local orientation sets Z_s at the vertices of a pseudoline arrangement, defined from oriented pseudolines avoiding s, with transport along edges and a consistency axiom (A9)
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial model of the orientation double cover / orientation local system of RP^2; closely related to chirotopes of rank-3 oriented matroids
ideas.usually_credited_to: Oriented matroids: Bland–Las Vergnas, Folkman–Lawrence (1978) topological representation; chirotopes: Dress, Bokowski et al.

ideas.what: Defining edge transport by going around a triangle of the 3-line sub-arrangement {Θ, D, D'}
ideas.modern_name: Use of triangles / local sub-arrangements (rank-3 'triangle' reasoning, mutations)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in pseudoline arrangement theory (Levi, Grünbaum, Ringel)

ideas.what: Identification of pencils and near-pencils as exceptional arrangements
ideas.modern_name: Near-pencil (the degenerate arrangement in Sylvester–Gallai type results)

deep.surprise_reason: A routine technical patch for a degenerate case in a combinatorial encoding of local orientations on a pseudoline arrangement. It is unfinished and explicitly unverified, and the ideas (orientation local system, triangles, near-pencil exceptions) are standard in oriented-matroid and arrangement theory.
transcription_corrections: First line: the '∃' carries a slash, i.e. it is '∄' (there is NO pseudoline avoiding both s and s'), not a deleted ∃: 'traiter le cas (très particulier !) où ∄ ps. droite qui ne passe par s ni par s''.
'≠Θ' in line 3 is an insertion qualifying D (D ≠ Θ passing through s), not a property of Θ.
'b une des orientations' should probably read 'b une des arêtes [of K'] qui joignent s à t', with 'l'unique arête b' de K'', since b and b' are segments of K'.
'On suppose que K est par réduite à' is likely 'On suppose que K n'est pas réduit à une famille de n≥3 ps. droites concourantes'.
'biguë' is probably 'digone' (cf. next page: 'une ps droite qui est une digone').
